report.incidentSummary: On 2026-10-16 starting at 05:10 UTC (10:40 IST), auth-service OTP success rate dropped sharply from ~97.4% to ~71%, resulting in approximately 30% of OTP login attempts failing. Investigation ruled out shared cache degradation, message queue processing lag, and notification-service API dispatch failures. However, the root cause cannot be conclusively proven due to missing downstream telecom delivery receipt latency metrics and an auth-service log shipping blackout that began at 04:54 UTC following an agent upgrade.
report.rootCauseStatement: The cause of the OTP success rate drop cannot be conclusively established. The leading hypothesis is upstream telecom delivery delays exceeding the 240-second OTP TTL (shortened on Oct 14 in CHG-48224), but delivery receipt (DLR) latency metrics are not collected and success rates lack telecom operator attribution. The alternative hypothesis of auth-service instance disruption or clock skew following the 04:54 UTC log-shipper upgrade (CHG-48221) cannot be verified due to a logging blackout after 04:54 UTC and absence of host-level NTP telemetry.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream telecom routing degradation or operator delivery delays causing OTP SMS messages to arrive after the 240-second OTP validity window (configured in CHG-48224), causing verification failures when users submit expired codes.
hypotheses.rationale: Matches historical incident PIR-1602 where carrier delivery lag caused OTP verification failures. sms-provider promptly accepted requests (HTTP 202) within ~120 ms, and the OTP TTL was recently shortened from 300s to 240s in CHG-48224. However, carrier DLR latency and operator-level metric labels are missing.

hypotheses.cause: The log-shipper agent upgrade on auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC (CHG-48221) caused node-level clock skew or instance state inconsistency, causing valid OTPs to be rejected during verification.
hypotheses.rationale: An infrastructure change (CHG-48221) on auth-service completed at 04:54 UTC, exactly when auth-service logging stopped completely. If the upgrade disturbed node clocks, time-based OTP validation could fail. However, onset occurred 16 minutes later at 05:10 UTC, auth-service p95 latency remained steady at ~300 ms, and host clock metrics are unavailable.

hypotheses.cause: notification-service dispatch failure or SMS provider rejecting outgoing SMS messages at the API level.
hypotheses.rationale: notification-service error rate stayed flat at ~0.30%, p95 latency was flat at ~120 ms, sms_send_failures remained at baseline (~3/min), and logs confirmed continuous HTTP 202 acceptances by sms-provider.

hypotheses.cause: message-queue backlog or consumer lag delaying asynchronous notification delivery.
hypotheses.rationale: Queue depth for notifications and debits stayed constant at baseline (~110-130 messages), and consumer lag remained stable at ~2.1 seconds throughout the window.

hypotheses.cause: Cache memory pressure, eviction spikes, or keyspace degradation causing premature eviction of OTP secrets.
hypotheses.rationale: Cache hit rates across all keyspaces remained between 92% and 95%, and cache evictions remained flat at baseline (~35 evictions/min) with no spikes.

facts.statement: auth-service otp_success_rate dropped from 97.44% at 05:05 UTC to 87.04% at 05:10 UTC and settled around 70-72% through 07:00 UTC.
auth-service otp_sent_per_min surged from ~1,000/min to a peak of 1,285/min between 05:10 UTC and 05:25 UTC before returning to ~1,030-1,050/min.
auth-service log-shipper agent was upgraded from v2.8 to v3.0 in CHG-48221 at 04:54 UTC on 2026-10-16.
auth-service logs completely ceased appearing in the central log store after 04:54:07 UTC, with 0 logs recorded between 05:00 UTC and 07:00 UTC.
auth-service p95 latency remained steady between 273 ms and 318 ms between 04:30 UTC and 07:00 UTC.
Config change CHG-48224 reduced auth-service otp.expiry_s from 300 seconds to 240 seconds on 2026-10-14 at 09:30 UTC.
notification-service latency_p95_ms remained between 110.8 ms and 126.2 ms, and error_rate remained between 0.24% and 0.37% across the entire window.
notification-service logged 308 successful 'sms accepted by sms-provider (template=otp)' events with HTTP 202 status and zero SMS dispatch errors between 04:30 UTC and 07:00 UTC.
cache hit rate across all keyspaces remained between 92% and 95%, and eviction rate stayed flat between 31 and 42 count/min.
message-queue queue depths and consumer lag remained stable at ~2.1 seconds with no message backlogs.

inferences.statement: The spike in otp_sent_per_min between 05:10 UTC and 05:25 UTC was caused by users retrying login requests after their initial OTP verification failed.
The log-shipper v3.0 upgrade (CHG-48221) broke auth-service log forwarding at 04:54 UTC, creating an observability blackout during the incident onset.
notification-service and the internal message queue did not contribute to OTP failures, as requests were accepted and handed off to sms-provider without delay or elevated error rates.

assumptions.statement: External carrier network delivery delays caused OTP SMS messages to arrive after the 240-second validity window had elapsed for a subset of mobile numbers.
Users entered the received OTP codes after expiration, prompting auth-service to reject them as invalid or expired.

CHG-48221 completed, upgrading log-shipper agent v2.8 to v3.0 on auth-service node pool.

confidence.rationale: Internal systems (cache, message queue, notification-service) are ruled out by definitive telemetry. However, differentiating between upstream telecom delivery lag (H2) and node-level clock/verification drift (H1) is prevented by the absence of carrier delivery receipt metrics and the auth-service logging blackout.

gaps.impact: Prevented inspection of auth-service OTP verification error codes (e.g., OTP_EXPIRED vs OTP_MISMATCH) and stack traces.

gaps.description: Delivery receipt (DLR) latency metrics and carrier delivery receipts are not ingested or tracked in notification-service.
gaps.impact: Prevents verifying whether SMS delivery times exceeded the 240-second OTP TTL.

gaps.description: auth-service otp_success_rate does not support telecom operator grouping, and host NTP clock drift metrics are missing.
gaps.impact: Cannot confirm operator-specific degradation or verify node clock synchronization.

recommendedActions.action: Investigate and resolve the auth-service log-shipper v3.0 failure (CHG-48221) or rollback log-shipper to v2.8 to restore auth-service application logs.
recommendedActions.rationale: auth-service log ingestion halted at 04:54 UTC, blinding operators to verification failure reasons.
recommendedActions.verification: Check query_logs for auth-service and verify active INFO, WARN, and ERROR streams resume.

recommendedActions.action: Temporarily revert auth-service otp.expiry_s from 240s to 300s (or 600s).
recommendedActions.rationale: If carrier delivery latency is elevated between 3 and 5 minutes (as seen in PIR-1602), increasing the TTL will allow delayed SMS OTPs to validate successfully.
recommendedActions.verification: Monitor auth-service otp_success_rate to observe if success rate recovers back toward >95%.

recommendedActions.action: Engage primary SMS provider support to audit carrier routing delays and evaluate failing over to the secondary SMS provider.
recommendedActions.rationale: PIR-2004 and PIR-1602 demonstrate that carrier-level degradations require provider rerouting or secondary failover.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify carrier delivery receipt latency reports from the provider and compare OTP success rates post-failover.

recommendedActions.action: Implement delivery receipt (DLR) latency tracking and export telecom operator labels on auth-service and notification-service metrics.
recommendedActions.rationale: Enables immediate automated detection of downstream telecom delivery lag without relying on external provider status pages.
recommendedActions.verification: Query notification-service metrics catalog for delivery_receipt_latency_p95_s and confirm presence.
